_comment: Field journal fish: real Swan River and Perth coast species. water: where they live (river: the Swan and Canning above the Narrows; estuary: the lower river, Fremantle harbour and the moles; ocean: beaches, groynes and reef). hours: [[from, to], ...] (to < from wraps past midnight). length: [min, max] cm, weighted to the small end; legal: WA minimum length in cm (0: none), undersized fish go back. kg = k * (cm / 10)^3. pay: anglers' club prize money per kg (WA doesn't allow selling a recreational catch). fight 0..1: how hard it pulls; shy 0..1: how short the strike window is. method: line, or net for crabs. junk: not a fish. model: body plan in scripts/field/fish_models.gd.

fish.name: Blowfish
fish.hint: Anywhere you drop a bait. It'll find you first.
fish.note: The blowie: bait thief, line biter, wharf pest. Nobody's ever been happy to see one. Back it goes.

fish.name: Black bream
fish.hint: Jetty pylons and snags up the river, at dusk and through the night.
fish.note: Wary, clever and the Swan River's own. They hang about the pylons and take a bait slowly, then go hard for cover.

fish.name: Tailor
fish.hint: Dawn and dusk, where the gulls are working the water.
fish.note: Run in schools through the river mouth and along the beaches at first and last light. Teeth like a tailor's shears.

fish.name: Australian herring
fish.note: The ruff, or tommy rough. Every kid's first fish off the Freo moles.

fish.name: Yellowfin whiting
fish.hint: Shallow sandy flats on a warm day: Point Walter, Canning Bridge.
fish.note: Sand-coloured and skittish, nosing the shallows for worms. Sweet eating, so the club pays well.

fish.name: Bar-tailed flathead
fish.hint: Lying in the sand on the river flats. Bump a lure along the bottom.
fish.note: All head and patience, buried in the sand until something swims over. Mind the spines.

fish.name: Tarwhine
fish.note: A silver bream with gold lines down its sides and yellow fins. Fights well above its size.

fish.name: Skippy
fish.hint: The moles and the groynes, any time there's light.
fish.note: Silver trevally to the books, skippy to everyone on the mole. Pulls far harder than it has any right to.

fish.name: Southern garfish
fish.hint: Just under the surface off the jetties and moles, in daylight.
fish.note: A needle with fins: a long lower jaw tipped in red. Nibbles, then is gone.

fish.name: Southern calamari
fish.hint: Under the jetty lights at night, on the moles and the harbour.
fish.note: Drawn to the lights after dark. Ink everywhere when it comes up, mostly on you.

fish.name: Mulloway
fish.hint: Deep holes in the river, after dark. Bring patience.
fish.note: The river's ghost. Big, silver and patient, and gone again before you're sure it was there. Locals fish a whole winter for one.

fish.name: Pink snapper
fish.hint: Off the moles at night, on the bottom. Mostly undersized; once in a while, not.
fish.note: Pink with bright blue spots. Most off the moles are little ones that go back; the big old ones live out in Cockburn Sound.

fish.name: King George whiting
fish.hint: Over sand and weed off the beaches and the groynes.
fish.note: Spotted brown on fawn. The best-eating whiting there is, so the club's prize money is generous.

fish.name: Blue manna crab
fish.hint: Drop a crab net off a river jetty and wait. Summer's best.
fish.note: Blue mannas: the river's summer ritual. Width across the shell, not counting the spines, must be 12.7 cm or it goes back.

fish.name: A Fiat hubcap
fish.hint: Somewhere in the river, off the Esplanade.
fish.note: A chrome Fiat 500 hubcap, 1970s, furred with weed. How did that get in the river?

fish.name: A bream with a tag in its jaw
fish.note: An old black bream with a yellow plastic tag through its jaw, sun-bleached nearly white. The tag reads FISHERIES WA 1979, No. 0015.
fish.page: 3 March 1979. Tagged a bream off the Mends Street jetty for the Fisheries survey, number 0015, and let it go under the lights. They say a bream can live twenty years if the river lets it. If you've caught it, it came back to the jetty. Let it go again. It always comes back to the jetty.
